facts.claim: Error tracking issue lifecycle events are produced by two independent paths that must be kept in sync: manual mutations go through `products/error_tracking/backend/logic/lifecycle_events.py:prepare_issue_lifecycle_event` (which builds `properties` dict and `AlertDeliveryWorkflowInputs`), while ingestion-driven transitions (created/reopened/spiking) go through `products/error_tracking/backend/temporal/lifecycle/side_effects.py:produce_issue_lifecycle_internal_event` and `alert_delivery_inputs`. Both independently compute an `assignee` (and now `assignee_name`) property from the same compact JSON assignee string (`{"type":...,"id":...}`), and the alert filter evaluator in `products/error_tracking/backend/temporal/alerts/filtering.py` (LIFECYCLE_PROPERTY_KEYS) must also know about any new key added to this property set, or filters referencing it will silently fail closed.
facts.evidence: "the triggering exception's properties are flattened under the lifecycle event's own properties" (filtering.py docstring); `assignee_property`/`assignee_name_property` are defined once in `lifecycle_events.py` and imported into `side_effects.py` to keep both producers consistent; `LIFECYCLE_PROPERTY_KEYS` in filtering.py lists `"assignee"` as a decidable key.

facts.claim: The error tracking alert destination's assignee property is a compact JSON string, not a structured object: `{"type":"user","id":<int>}` or `{"type":"role","id":"<uuid-string>"}`, byte-identical to cymbal's (rust) serde output so exact-match HogQL filters work across both ingestion-driven and manual transitions. It is absent entirely (not null) on unassigned issues.
facts.evidence: "Wire-compatible with cymbal's `Assignee` serialization on created/reopened events (compact serde JSON, adjacently tagged, numeric user ids and string role ids)" in `assignee_property`; test: `assert event.properties["assignee"] == f'{{"type":"user","id":{self.user.id}}}'`; unassign test asserts `"assignee" not in event.properties`.

facts.claim: The `authoring-error-tracking-alerts` skill's reference doc (`references/event-triggers.md`) is the canonical place the AI assistant reads for what alert event properties templates can use; it previously didn't describe `assignee`/`assignee_name` shape at all, forcing guesses. Any new lifecycle event property intended for template use must be documented there (format, absent-when-unassigned behavior) or the authoring assistant won't know it exists.
